title: Adaptive Latency-Anomaly Quorum for Region Arbitration and Tiered Variant Demotion
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Region selection currently uses static percentile thresholds (p50/p95) and a separate network health flag. This leads to noisy flip-flopping during short-lived spikes and slow reaction to persistent degradations. We need a single, interpretable arbitration mechanism that: 1) detects real latency anomalies using percentile drift and burst signatures, 2) penalizes network-path issues (packet loss/timeout rate) separately but combinable, 3) supports tier-aware routing (hosted/dedicated/private) and cost-weighted preferences, and 4) demotes model variants (e.g., quantized / distil) gracefully when primary variant is unhealthy.
proposal_summary: Introduce "Anomaly-Weighted Latency Quorum" (AWLQ): a composite score per region that fuses percentile drift (delta p50/p95 vs baseline), EWMA-stabilized latency percentiles, and a path-quality penalty derived from packet loss and TCP timeout rates. AWLQ produces a ranked quorum of candidate regions; routing picks the highest-ranked region within customer tier constraints. Additionally, AWLQ emits a "variant_demote_signal" when a region's score drops below a demotion threshold for a sustained cooldown window; that signal triggers tiered fallback to a preconfigured model variant instead of immediate global failover.
technical_design:
Core components:
- Baselines: maintain per-region baseline p50 and p95 distributions over a rolling 24h window (histogram summary).
- Drift detector: compute delta_p50 = current_p50 - baseline_p50 and delta_p95 likewise; apply significance test using bootstrapped CI to avoid reacting to sampling noise.
- Stabilizer: apply short-window EWMA (alpha configurable by tier) on percentile values to smooth single-sample jitter while preserving burst detection.
- Path penalty: derive PathQuality = 1 - min(1, scaled(packet_loss_rate * loss_weight + tcp_timeouts * timeout_weight)); penalty multiplies AWLQ score.
- Cost bias: incorporate cost-tier multiplier to prefer cheaper region variants only when score differences are within a configurable epsilon.
- Quorum logic: select top-N regions where AWLQ < threshold. If top region is outside customer tier (e.g., dedicated-only), fall back to highest-scoring within tier.
- Variant demotion: if AWLQ for a region remains below demote_threshold for demote_window (e.g., 5m), emit variant_demote_signal with severity. Demotion stages: soft-demote (lowered concurrency/burst allowance), hard-demote (switch to fallback model variant). Auto-heal after recovery + coolup window.
- Safety: implement hysteresis (cooldown and grace counters) and minimum-sample enforcement to avoid reacting to small traffic segments.
- Observability: expose AWLQ components (baseline drift, EWMA, path penalty, quorum rank, demote state) in per-region telemetry and per-request routing decision metadata.
acceptance_criteria: AWLQ score computed for all active regions with per-minute updates and visible in routing decisions metadata
False positive demotions <= 1 per 10k routing decisions during controlled fault-injection tests
Total % of requests routed to non-preferred tier decreases by >= 60% during transient spikes compared to baseline flip-flop behavior
Variant demotion and auto-heal observed in canary runs with injected packet loss: demote triggers within configured demote_window and reverses after recovery + coolup
No >5% regression in successful request rate or median latency on primary traffic during rollout canary (10% traffic)
rollout_plan: 1) Unit tests + simulation harness for AWLQ scoring: deterministic input -> expected ranking
2) Staging deploy guarded by feature flag; run with shadow routing for 72 hours (compare AWLQ decisions to current router)
3) Canary: enable decision path for 10% of traffic for a mix of tenants (hosted + dedicated) for 48 hours; monitor metrics and error budgets
4) Gradual ramp to 50% with rollback gates based on SLOs and demotion FP rate
5) Full rollout conditional on canary success and post-mortem review
telemetry_queries: query:awlaq_region_scores: average AWLQ per region over last 1m and 5m windows
query:variant_demote_events: count variant_demote_signal by region and severity over last 7d
query:flipflop_rate: count region change events per route per hour
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed - simulation harness can replay regional latency traces and output rankings. Found initial sensitivity to sample count; added min-sample threshold.

2026-02-20: Implemented EWMA stabilizer and path penalty prototype; integration tests green locally.
Note: tuned EWMA alpha per tier (hosted=0.3, dedicated=0.15).
2026-02-28: Staging deploy with shadowing started. Observed 2% of routes where AWLQ prefers farther low-cost region due to cost bias; reduced cost epsilon from 10ms to 3ms.
2026-03-03: Canary flag created; QA to run fault-injection for packet loss scenarios on 2026-03-06. Preparing rollback runbook and SRE alert thresholds.
qa_notes: QA to run the routing simulator with historical spikes (holiday traffic and seeded outages) and validate demotion FP rate <= 1/10k. Include tests for tier constraints and cost-bias behavior. Perform integration test with Dedicated autoscaler to ensure demotion doesn't cause capacity thrash.
notes_on_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs considered: aggressive sensitivity detects more true positives but increases false-positive demotions causing unnecessary variant switching. We favor a conservative default (longer EWMA + min-sample) and provide a per-customer override. Cost-bias reduces unit cost at the risk of slight latency increase for tail-sensitive customers; we expose the epsilon and recommend conservative defaults for SLO-sensitive tenants.
